lines: {target}? Strange quiet can make a place feel too safe.
If anyone heads for Mushroom Fields, tell them. Eat only what you know and keep your boat close.
Mycelium underfoot is not village dirt.
The warning about steep shorelines around soft mycelium gives me a very different picture of Mushroom Fields.
I will remember Mushroom Fields as odd land where even the grass changed its mind.
I would not take another step until the group knew about steep shorelines around soft mycelium.
The part about mooshrooms wandering through purple grass in the rain is what I keep picturing.
I would not wait for trouble before leading everyone toward a hollow beside a giant red mushroom.
How did a sheltered landing where the boat cannot drift away help once it was time to turn back?
With sea fog covering the mushroom coast ahead, the tallest red mushroom near shore could vanish sooner than people expect.
Careful movement matters more than people think, especially around quiet islands covered in huge mushrooms and mycelium.
No reward keeps me there once deep water, cliffs, and getting stranded far from home begins.
Around Mushroom Fields, every watch keeper should know how to warn us about a mooshroom crowding the narrow path.
The flock would not need words to warn me about the mycelium hills of Mushroom Fields.
Nothing beside our pasture prepares a person for quiet islands covered in huge mushrooms and mycelium.
Anyone who gets lost should call from the tallest red mushroom near shore instead of wandering farther away.
I would slow the group before steep shorelines around soft mycelium turned one stumble into trouble.
The first village roof must have been a welcome sight after quiet islands covered in huge mushrooms and mycelium.
What made mushrooms and a glimpse of the strange mooshrooms worth all that trouble?
A shepherd carries feed for the flock. Travelers near Mushroom Fields deserve the same planning.
{target}? Open ground shows you to everything else.
If anyone heads for Plains, tell them. Keep moving and watch the horizon.
Grass bends before trouble arrives if you look.
The village road kept in sight sounds more valuable than treasure once you know what waits at Plains.
I will remember Plains as wide land with nowhere to hide after dark.
Across the open fields of Plains, I'd keep everyone close enough to hear a warning.
A zombie crossing the grass after dark is where my curiosity would end.
If every creature grew still near the open fields of Plains, so would I.
I would keep a spare wrap ready for the walk back from Plains.
An extra hour spent on a straight course between visible landmarks would be time well used.
The next traveler should hear about a low wall beside the village road before setting out for Plains.
I knew the name {target}. I did not picture wide grassland where the horizon never hides.
It took courage to face ravines, patrols, and night arriving without shelter and sense to know when to leave.
I would not take another step until the group knew about tall grass hiding shallow ravines.
Seeing you at the gate would finally quiet my worry about ravines, patrols, and night arriving without shelter.
A journey around wide grassland where the horizon never hides can outlast a food bag. Did yours?
I would make a low wall beside the village road our meeting place if the route forced us apart.
I would count everyone each time we passed the village road kept in sight.
Where could you turn when ravines, patrols, and night arriving without shelter closed the safer paths?
On the Plains, I would carry food and a bed while keeping a village or hill in sight.
{target}? Sunny fields can still point toward trouble.
If anyone heads for Sunflower Plains, tell them. Enjoy the flowers with a torch ready.
Sunflowers face light, not safety.
I will think of the sunflower rows pointing home whenever someone mentions Sunflower Plains now.
I will remember Sunflower Plains as bright fields that still grow dark at night.
I hope you carried food, a bed, and torches for the return. Going without it near open fields bright with sunflowers all facing one way sounds miserable.
Near Sunflower Plains, I would trust the flock if it refused the ground.
If anyone else goes, tell them to mark the return before following the flowers too far.
What warned you that hidden ravines, bees, and little cover after dark was about to become a problem?
I would not argue over packs with a zombie moving between the flowers at night nearby.
No rushing while a route checked before following the flowers too far is the way home.
Nobody should cross the tall sunflowers of Sunflower Plains alone after hearing that story.
Getting past hidden ravines, bees, and little cover after dark was no small thing.
I will remember the route by the sunflower rows pointing home, not by what anyone hoped to find.
A good warning names the real trouble, and this one names flowers hiding dips in the open ground.
I would mark the sunflower rows pointing home where everyone could see it.
A road past open fields bright with sunflowers all facing one way could empty a food bag quickly.
{target}? You found open fields bright with sunflowers all facing one way. I can see why that stayed with you.
I would check every boot and strap before setting out across the tall sunflowers of Sunflower Plains.
At a low wall beside a sunflower patch, I would check for sore feet, empty waterskins, and frayed straps.
